title: Nearest Meeting Cell
body:
A maze has N cells numbered 0 to N − 1. Each cell has at most one exit: edge[i] is the cell you reach by leaving cell i, or -1 if cell i has no exit.

Two people start at cells C1 and C2 and keep following exits. A cell is a meeting cell if both can reach it. Print the meeting cell with the smallest dist(C1, X) + dist(C2, X), where dist counts exits followed. Break ties by the smaller cell number. Print -1 if no cell is reachable from both.

The report did not say whether "nearest" means the sum or the maximum of the two distances; this mock uses the sum.

Function to complete

Complete nearestMeetingCell(edge, c1, c2). It returns the nearest meeting cell, or -1.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.

samples.ex: Both reach cell 2 in one step, total 2.
From 9: 8, 0, 4 (distance 3). From 2: 1, 4 (distance 2). Total 5 at cell 4 is the smallest.

lc: 2359 Find Closest Node to Given Two Nodes

    edge = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_n)])); _p += (_n)
    c1 = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    c2 = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _r = Solution().nearestMeetingCell(edge, c1, c2)
